Calories Burned Calculator

Calories burned depend mainly on your weight, how long you exercise and how intense the activity is. A 70 kg person burns roughly 130 kcal in 30 minutes of easy walking and about 360 kcal in 30 minutes of running at 10 km/h. Choose an activity to see your own estimate.

Everything runs in your browser. Nothing you type is sent anywhere.

How it's calculated: METs

Every activity has a MET value (metabolic equivalent of task): how much energy it uses compared with sitting still. Sitting is about 1 MET; running at 10 km/h is about 9.8 METs, nearly ten times as much. The values here come from the Compendium of Physical Activities, the standard reference used in exercise research.

Calories burned = MET × 3.5 × weight (kg) ÷ 200 × minutes Example: running at 10 km/h (MET 9.8), 70 kg, 30 minutes 9.8 × 3.5 × 70 ÷ 200 × 30 = 360 kcal

Why heavier people burn more

Moving a heavier body takes more energy, so the same walk burns more calories for someone who weighs 90 kg than for someone who weighs 60 kg. That's also why calorie burn per session falls a little as you lose weight.

Keep it in perspective

Exercise burns fewer calories than most people expect: a 30-minute run is roughly a large slice of cake. For weight loss, diet usually matters more, but exercise brings huge benefits for heart health, mood, sleep and keeping muscle. Most health bodies recommend at least 150 minutes of moderate activity a week plus muscle-strengthening twice a week.

Accuracy

MET values are averages. Fitter people are more efficient and may burn a little less for the same activity; hills, wind and effort level change the burn too. Smartwatches estimate using heart rate, which helps, but studies show they often overestimate calories.

Frequently asked questions

How many calories does walking burn?

About 3.5 METs at 5 km/h: roughly 130 kcal per 30 minutes for a 70 kg person.

How many calories does running burn?

Running at 10 km/h burns about 360 kcal per 30 minutes for a 70 kg person.

What is a MET?

A metabolic equivalent: the energy cost of an activity compared with sitting still (1 MET).

Are fitness tracker calorie numbers accurate?

They’re rough estimates and often overestimate calories burned, especially for activities other than walking and running.

Which exercise burns the most calories?

Vigorous activities such as running, jump rope, fast cycling and swimming laps burn the most per minute.
